description: Marketplace review requirements that apply to a Designer Extension-only App (no Data Client, no Webflow OAuth scopes, no Install URL, no code injected into customer sites). Every rule carries a provenance tag and names the layer that enforces it. A rule enforced only by 'human' is a gate the generator checklists but cannot verify.

provenance.published: Stated as a requirement on developers.webflow.com (Marketplace Guidelines, Submitting your App, Listing your App, Designer Extension docs) as of the date in `version`.
provenance.control: A security or engineering control that prepares review evidence and generalizes recurring review risk. Not verbatim published policy. Same label the preflight skill and toolkit use.
provenance.reviewer-practice: Enforced in actual reviews (Jul-Sep 2026 rejection corpus, 532 versions) but not written in the published docs. Encoded here because this tool is internal. The 8/17 changelog promise is 'if it isn't published we don't hold your submission to it', so a public tool must not present these as requirements.

severity.blocker: Reviewers reject on sight, or the upload fails before review starts.
severity.required: Reviewers return the submission for changes.
severity.suggested: Reviewers may flag it; fixing it removes a conversation.

enforcedBy.template: The compliant scaffold makes the violation hard to write.
enforcedBy.doctor: `wf-forge doctor` checks the built bundle.zip and review-artifacts.
enforcedBy.listing-kit: `wf-forge listing` checks listing copy, assets, and URLs.
enforcedBy.preflight: App Review Preflight (the Designer Extension that issues wfpre_ receipts).
enforcedBy.form: The submission form at developers.webflow.com/submit validates it.
enforcedBy.human: A person must do or confirm it. The packet lists these as gates.

sources.FORM: webflow/wf-app-form-cloud lib/ (vendored under src/vendor/form-rules, see VENDOR.json)

requirements.title: webflow.json declares name, apiVersion "2", and publicDir
The manifest name and page title are the real product name, not a scaffold default
bundle.zip contains exactly one webflow.json
The bundled webflow.json carries no CLI telemetry block
requirements.note: Packaging hygiene written by Webflow CLI 2.3.0 and earlier. Not a security finding and not evidence of a development build.

requirements.title: bundle.zip is 5 MB or smaller
requirements.note: An oversized bundle fails at upload, before review starts.

requirements.title: No .map files or inline data: source maps inside bundle.zip
requirements.note: Source maps go in the form's private upload, never in the artifact that ships to customers.

requirements.title: A version-3 source map for each minified bundle file exists in review-artifacts/ and is attached to the form's private upload
requirements.note: Required when the submission ships a new or changed minified bundle. The gap analysis notes the docs say 'required' on the submission page and 'may request' on the guidelines page; this tool uses the stricter reading.

requirements.title: Production build: no eval-based module wrappers, no framework error-decoder URLs, no dev-server or hot-update residue
No eval(), new Function(), or string-argument timers
No credentials, private keys, or client secrets in the bundle
No inline event handlers or javascript: URLs in the extension HTML
No inline <script> blocks; all script is in bundled files
No inline <style> blocks or runtime style injection; styles live in a stylesheet file
requirements.note: 74 feedback texts in the Jul-Sep corpus cite inline styles; DOC-53 lists only inline handlers, javascript: URLs, and unsafe-eval. The template avoids style-loader so this never comes up.

requirements.title: The extension loads no script from a host outside the bundle
requirements.note: Remotely loaded code can change after approval. A stylesheet or font from a named host is acceptable if declared in review notes.

requirements.title: No localhost, staging, or tunnel host used as a request destination
requirements.note: A bare 'localhost' literal in a library's URL fallback is not residue. Only a localhost URL with a port or path, or a tunnel host, is reported.

requirements.title: No externally hosted iframe as the primary App UI
requirements.note: Iframes are fine for third-party authentication flows.

requirements.title: No direct DOM manipulation of the Designer; Designer APIs only
Sections are identified with getTag() === 'section', not element.type === 'Section'
requirements.note: Preset-created sections report type 'Block'. The published set-tag example still teaches the broken pattern.

requirements.title: No tokens or secrets written to localStorage or sessionStorage, and none placed in URLs
requirements.note: Ordinary UI preferences in localStorage are fine.

requirements.title: No alert(), confirm(), or prompt(); use webflow.notify
The App changes nothing in the site until the user acts
requirements.note: 54 versions cited 'state change without user interaction'. The template's only mutating path is a click handler. Confirm in the demo video.

requirements.title: No keyboard shortcut invokes the App
Any analytics inside the extension runs only after the user consents
requirements.note: 81 versions cited analytics or tracking without consent. The template ships a consent gate with no SDK wired in.

requirements.title: Every third-party dependency in the bundle can be named; lockfile and production manifest available on request
Visual style uses Webflow's published App colors and typography; 4px spacing rhythm
Accessible: alt text, keyboard navigation, sufficient contrast, visible focus
App runs end to end with no crashes and no placeholder content or test data
App name is 30 characters or fewer and does not use Webflow marks
Short description is 100 characters or fewer and states the value proposition
Long description is 10,000 characters or fewer, Markdown without links, specific about what the App does
At most 5 listed features
One or two categories from the published list
requirements.note: The listing doc says up to 5; the form accepts at most 2. The form is the gate.

requirements.title: Copy describes the App's own behavior: no unverifiable claims, beta language, agency pitch, third-party brand confusion, staging markers, or script tags
Listing copy is in English
Description, screenshots, and demo video match actual behavior
App icon is a 900x900 PNG, 50 KB or smaller, a logomark rather than a text logotype, with alt text
requirements.note: The guidelines page separately says 512x512. Produce 900x900 so it downsizes cleanly; the form enforces 900.

requirements.title: 3 to 5 screenshots at 1280x846 showing real features, each with descriptive alt text
requirements.note: The listing doc recommends at least 4.

requirements.title: A 2 to 5 minute review demo video from install to usage, in English or with English subtitles, on a private link
requirements.note: Length and content cannot be checked from a URL. Separate from the optional 1-2 minute promo video.

requirements.title: Privacy policy and terms of service URLs are reachable HTTPS pages on a production host
Privacy policy and terms of service are distinct pages
requirements.note: The form calibration found 26 approved apps sharing one legal page, so this stays a suggestion.

requirements.title: The privacy policy actually covers what the App collects, where it is stored, and how it is used
requirements.note: This tool never authors legal text. It emits a disclosure outline for Legal or the developer to use.

requirements.title: Homepage URL is valid HTTPS on a production host
Documentation URL is provided and on a production host
Support email is valid and does not use Webflow marks
Every fee, subscription, or in-app purchase is disclosed; a Paid app explains its tiers in review notes
No advertisements in the App
Creator name is a real publisher, not a placeholder; no impersonation
Only one developer account is used
A published .webflow.io testing site with the App installed is entered in the form
Demo access is provided: demo account, full demo mode, or credentials to required resources
Two-factor authentication is enabled on an admin account of the submitting Workspace
App Review Preflight was run on the exact bundle and source-map artifact attached to the form, and its wfpre_ receipt is pasted in
The App is complete and production-ready; beta or pre-release Apps are not published
The App registers only the Designer Extension capability; it does not register as a Data Client to 'have OAuth'
requirements.note: Registering a Data Client brings OAuth scopes, an Install URL, backend auth, and uninstall cleanup into review. Those are the largest rejection families and this tool's scope excludes them.
